# UQDA Core v0.1.5

This release makes the command-line interface self-explanatory and launches the
official UQDA Core container package on GitHub Container Registry. It does not
change the wire protocol, identity/address derivation, configuration format, or
peer compatibility.

## Guided command-line help

- Running `uqda`, requesting help, or supplying an unknown option now shows
  task-oriented commands and a concrete example for every option.
- Identity queries clearly show that `-useconf` or `-useconffile` is required.
- Daemon-only and service-manager-only options are identified explicitly.
- Private-key export is accompanied by a safety warning.
- The help distinguishes UQDA Core from `uqdactl` and UQDA Stack functionality.

## Official container package

- Publishes `ghcr.io/uqda/uqda-core` as a public GitHub Container Registry package.
- Supports `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`, `linux/arm/v7`, and `linux/arm/v6`.
- Publishes `v0.1.5`, `0.1.5`, `0.1`, `0`, and `latest` tags; main publishes
  the rolling `edge` tag.
- Attaches an SBOM and maximum-mode build provenance to the multi-platform
  image.
- Verifies the manifest, performs an anonymous pull, runs the packaged binary,
  and checks its version before the GitHub release is created.

## Installation

```sh
docker pull ghcr.io/uqda/uqda-core:latest
docker run --rm -it \
  --cap-add=NET_ADMIN \
  --device=/dev/net/tun \
  -v uqda-config:/etc/uqda \
  ghcr.io/uqda/uqda-core:latest
```

Native installers and portable archives remain available from the GitHub
release and continue to use SHA-256 checksums, Sigstore signing, and GitHub
provenance attestations.

UQDA remains an encrypted overlay rather than an anonymity system and has not
yet received an independent security audit. Keep the IPv6 firewall enabled and
protect the node configuration and administration endpoint.
